headline: Your Praxis EMR waterfall journey.
subheadline: One routed cascade that finds independent practices drowning in template charting, and hands each one the Praxis proof that fits their pain.
productSummary: Praxis EMR is a template-free, AI-driven EHR for solo to mid-sized independent practices. Its patented Concept Processing engine learns how each physician documents and charts in their own words, Reflective AI reconciles ambient speech with the doctor's prior clinical knowledge, and Datum+ automates MIPS, MACRA, ACO and eCQM reporting from the notes physicians already write.
coreInsight: Every EHR buyer is told their system is 'easy'. The practices that will actually switch are the ones already paying a visible price for template charting: a scribe job post, a weak MIPS score, or a pick-list EHR on their patient portal. Route on that price, lead with Praxis's physician-voted proof, and let the catch-all carry everyone else.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the price a practice already pays for template charting
sections.takeaway: A practice hiring scribes, losing MIPS points, or running a pick-list EHR is showing the cost of templates in public data. NPPES, CMS Care Compare, job boards and the practice's own patient-portal link expose it without paid enrichment.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: First match wins, top to bottom, catch-all underneath
sections.takeaway: Exclude existing Praxis users and health-system-owned clinics, then route: scribe hiring, then a below-threshold MIPS score, then a detected template EHR, then every other independent practice. Each practice lands in exactly one campaign.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Four tiers, hottest to broadest
sections.takeaway: Pain comes from the trigger (paying humans to chart, reporting penalties, click-heavy templates). Value props come straight from praxisemr.com: Concept Processing, Datum+, switch-in C-CDA import, and physician-voted satisfaction rankings.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: One campaign per tier, one offer per campaign
sections.takeaway: Office Managers and Practice Administrators get the operational angle (scribe cost, reporting, switching effort). Physician-owners get the clinical angle (chart in your own words, faster over time).

sections.label: Emails
sections.title: Three-touch sequences, notice line first
sections.takeaway: Day 0 names the observed signal, Day 3 rotates the value prop in-thread, Day 7 is the no-call ask: reply yes and we send the sheet. All proof lines are sourced from praxisemr.com.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Pull, route, send, then scale or cut on reply math
sections.takeaway: Build the NPPES + Care Compare TAM once, run the routing agent, launch tiers with at least ~1,500 contacts, and judge each on positive replies per send. Keep adding practices; do not rebuild the strategy.

signalReasons: Template pain is invisible in firmographics but visible in behavior: a scribe or transcription job post means the practice is paying people to make up for the EHR.
MIPS final scores are published by CMS per group and clinician, so reporting pain is observable and tied to real Medicare payment adjustments, which is what Datum+ automates.

The patient-portal link on a practice website (healow, athenaPatient, NextGen Patient Portal, FollowMyHealth, etc.) names the current EHR reliably, because the link only exists if the practice uses that system.
All three signals ride on free or cheap public data (NPPES, CMS Care Compare / QPP, job boards, a homepage scrape), so the TAM and the routing signal come in the same pull.

sources.name: NPPES NPI Registry (CMS, free bulk download)
sources.delivers: TAM gate: every U.S. organization NPI with physician taxonomy, practice address, phone, and the authorized official's name and title (often the physician-owner or practice administrator).

sources.name: CMS Care Compare: Doctors and Clinicians national file
sources.delivers: Group practice IDs, clinicians per group (provider_count), and hospital affiliations used to exclude health-system-owned clinics.

sources.name: CMS QPP / Care Compare MIPS public reporting
sources.delivers: MIPS final score and payment adjustment per group or clinician for the latest published performance year. Routing signal for Tier 2.

sources.name: Indeed + LinkedIn Jobs scrape
sources.delivers: Open roles in the last 60 days titled medical scribe, remote scribe, medical transcriptionist, chart prep or clinical documentation specialist. Routing signal for Tier 1.

sources.name: Google Maps + practice homepage scrape
sources.delivers: Practice website and the patient-portal link that names the current EHR (current_ehr), plus Praxis portal detection for the exclusion rule. Routing signal for Tier 3.

sources.name: Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Navigator
sources.delivers: Verified emails for Office Manager, Practice Manager, Practice Administrator and physician-owner contacts at each routed practice.

routingRules.if: praxis_customer = true (Praxis portal or Praxis named on site)
routingRules.why: Already a Praxis practice. Route to Praxis account management, not cold outbound.

routingRules.if: health_system_affiliation = owned / employed (Epic MyChart under a hospital domain, or group billed under a health system)
routingRules.why: Praxis's own comparison notes less presence in large hospital systems. Employed physicians do not choose their EHR.
The practice is paying people to absorb charting time. Strongest, most time-bound intent.

routingRules.if: ELSE IF mips_final_score below the CMS performance threshold OR mips_payment_adjustment negative (latest published year)
routingRules.why: Reporting is costing Medicare revenue. Datum+ automates MIPS, MACRA, ACO and eCQM reporting from the physician's own text.

routingRules.if: ELSE IF current_ehr in {eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen, Greenway, Veradigm/Allscripts, Practice Fusion, Amazing Charts, other template-based ambulatory EHR}
routingRules.why: Named template EHR on the portal link. Switch framing: Praxis imports demographics from any EHR and transfers charts via C-CDA.

routingRules.if: ELSE (every remaining independent practice in the TAM)
routingRules.then: Tier 4: Catch-all, chart in your own words
routingRules.why: Covers 100% of the TAM. Broad Concept Processing plus physician-rating proof, softest ask.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Scribe spend
tiers.trigger: Independent practice posted a medical scribe, remote scribe, transcriptionist, chart-prep or clinical documentation role in the last 60 days (Indeed / LinkedIn Jobs).
tiers.pain: They are adding headcount just to keep up with the chart. Every scribe hire is a recurring cost created by an EHR that makes physicians document through templates and clicks.
tiers.valueProp: Concept Processing learns each physician's clinical concepts and documentation patterns so charting gets faster the more they use it, and Reflective AI reconciles ambient speech with the doctor's own prior knowledge (praxisemr.com).
tiers.magnet: Scribe-or-software worksheet (practice plugs in its own scribe cost vs a Praxis license) + 2-minute Concept Processing walkthrough
tiers.dataSource: Indeed + LinkedIn Jobs scrape matched to NPPES organization NPI

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: MIPS gap
tiers.trigger: Latest published CMS MIPS final score below the performance threshold, or a negative payment adjustment, for the group or its clinicians.
tiers.pain: Quality reporting is costing Medicare revenue, usually because the data sits in free text the current EHR cannot count unless someone re-enters it in templates.
tiers.valueProp: Datum+ embeds discrete data inside the physician's own text and automates MIPS, MACRA, ACO and eCQM reporting, 'without turning medical providers into data-entry clerks' (praxisemr.com).
tiers.magnet: MIPS gap sheet: which of their reported measures Datum+ captures from notes they already write
tiers.dataSource: CMS QPP / Care Compare MIPS public reporting joined on group PAC ID + NPI
tiers.replyDensity: High. Money-linked pain with a public number (estimate)

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Template EHR switch
tiers.trigger: Practice website patient-portal link names a template-based ambulatory EHR (healow/eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, NextGen, Greenway, Veradigm/Allscripts, Practice Fusion, Amazing Charts, etc.).
tiers.pain: Pick-list templates force physicians to describe complex visits in someone else's words, which costs time per note and produces cloned-looking documentation.
tiers.valueProp: The only template-free EHR: chart in your own words, in any specialty. Switching is built in: demographics import from any EHR, full charts via C-CDA, 20 hours of initial training included with a new license (praxisemr.com).
tiers.magnet: {{current_ehr}}-to-Praxis switch sheet + AAFP 'physicians who switched EHRs' results
tiers.dataSource: Google Maps + homepage scrape for portal links, matched to NPPES
tiers.replyDensity: Medium. Named competitor, no urgency trigger (estimate)

tiers.name: Tier 4
tiers.label: Catch-all: chart in your own words
tiers.trigger: Every remaining independent practice in the TAM (no scribe post, no MIPS gap, EHR not detected or not on the list).
tiers.pain: Charting still eats the physician's evenings; most EHRs digitized the paper record instead of helping the doctor think.
tiers.valueProp: Praxis thinks like the physician and gets faster with use. Ranked #1 of 349 vendors by 5,700 providers in 1-5 physician offices (Black Book) and 4.73/5 with AmericanEHR Partners (Dec 2021).
tiers.magnet: Template-free charting one-pager + AmericanEHR Partners 2021 ratings PDF

campaigns.name: Scribe job post: software vs headcount
campaigns.strategy: Notice the {{scribe_job_title}} post on {{job_board}}, ask whether the hire is really about charting load, and offer the worksheet that compares their own scribe cost to Concept Processing. Send to Office Manager first, physician-owner on Day 7.
campaigns.overview: Smallest, hottest tier. Refill weekly from job boards; launch once ~1,500 contacts accumulate, otherwise fold new rows into Tier 3 copy.

campaigns.name: MIPS score: automate the reporting
campaigns.strategy: Reference the published {{mips_year}} MIPS score of {{mips_score}}, poke at re-entering data for reporting, and offer the MIPS gap sheet showing what Datum+ captures from existing notes.
campaigns.overview: Practice Administrator / Office Manager is the buyer. Public CMS number makes the notice line undeniable without sounding creepy.

campaigns.name: Template EHR: the switch sheet
campaigns.strategy: Name {{current_ehr}} from the {{portal_name}} portal link, ask whether notes still come out of pick-lists, and offer the switch sheet (import, C-CDA transfer, included training) plus AAFP switcher results.
campaigns.overview: Largest named-competitor pool. A/B physician-owner (own words, faster over time) vs Office Manager (switching effort, training included).

campaigns.name: Catch-all: practice medicine your way
campaigns.strategy: Billboard opener on template-free charting for {{specialty}} practices, backed by Black Book and AmericanEHR rankings, soft resource CTA.
campaigns.overview: Guarantees 100% TAM coverage. Softest ask; winners here get promoted into new tier variants.

launchPlan: Pull the TAM: NPPES organization NPIs with physician taxonomies, joined to the CMS Doctors and Clinicians file for provider_count and hospital affiliation. Keep independent practices with roughly 1-25 clinicians.
Enrich once: homepage + Google Maps scrape for the patient-portal link (current_ehr, praxis_customer), CMS MIPS public reporting for score and adjustment, 60-day Indeed/LinkedIn scribe job scrape.
Run the routing agent top to bottom: exclusions, Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, catch-all. Assert every practice exits with exactly one tier.
Find contacts per practice via Apollo / Sales Navigator: Office Manager or Practice Administrator first, physician-owner second (for the Day 7 'you or {{alt_decision_maker}}' line).
Have Praxis approve the four offers (worksheet, MIPS gap sheet, switch sheet, one-pager) and every proof line before sends start.
Launch only tiers with ~1,500+ contacts. Tier 1 accumulates weekly; until it clears ~1,500, send new scribe-hiring rows through Tier 3 copy.
Review reply math per tier after 1,500 sends, scale or cut per thresholds, then keep adding NPPES practices without rebuilding the strategy.
